# Draft:C. Edward Coffey MD

----
C. Edward Coffey MD (born May 11, 1952) is an American physician executive and clinical scientist.  Coffey is an accomplished physician (board certified in both Neurology and Psychiatry) with expertise in neuropsychiatry and brain stimulation treatment, garnering numerous listings as a “Top Doctor.”  Coffey has made important scientific contributions to the fields of neuropsychiatry, brain stimulation, suicide prevention, family-centered care, and healthcare quality improvement.   He has authored over 150 scientific publications and chapters, as well as several influential textbooks, and he serves on the editorial boards of several medical journals.  Coffey is also an award-winning health care executive, well known for creating and leading the “Perfect Depression Care” innovation and pioneering the audacious “Zero Suicide Model,” now the preferred suicide prevention approach for health systems throughout the US and in more than 30 countries worldwide.
BIOGRAPHY
Coffey earned his BS degree in Psychology from Wofford College (Phi Beta Kappa) in 1974, where he also won a [https://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/scholar-community/rhodes-scholar-database/ Rhodes Scholarship] to Oxford University (St. John's College; BA in Psychology, Philosophy, and Physiology, 1976).  He earned his MD from Duke University (AOA) in 1979, where he subsequently completed a medical internship and residencies in neurology and psychiatry (1984).  Coffey has held faculty and leadership positions at Duke University Medical Center (1984-1990), Allegheny University of the Health Sciences (1990-1996), Henry Ford Health System (System Vice President and Chair of Psychiatry, 1996-2014), The Menninger Clinic (President and CEO, 2014-2017), the Baylor College of Medicine (2014-2018), and the Medical University of South Carolina, Charleston, SC (2018-present).
Coffey is a Fellow and former President of both the American Neuropsychiatric Association (ANPA) and the International Society for ECT and Neurostimulation (ISEN). He is also a Distinguished Life Fellow of the American Psychiatric Association (APA), a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology (AAN), and a member of the American College of Psychiatrists (ACP).
